articles.title: When did football fans first start wearing replica kits? | The Knowledge
articles.summary: Plus: more costly (and beneficial) red cards, plus attacks with triple half-century of international goals. Mail us with your all of your questions and answers. “When did fans wearing replica kits become a thing?” asks Alex Ecob.
body: As the question suggests, this is a not a straightforward answer. Buckle up folks, as we veer wildly from copyright acts to academia, via multiple reports of unofficial kits, DIY jobs, cup-final special editions, youth strips, sew-on jobs and the like. But if we are to draw a line in the sand, and declare one date or one jersey as the first official, adult replica kit to be sold by a club to the general public (or at least those close enough to the club shop), then we probably have to give the gong to Leeds United in 1973, although only children’s sizes were produced initially.

“The first replica kit was produced by Admiral for Leeds United in 1973-74,” emails Chai from Atlanta. “History has it that Leeds’ manager, Don Revie, and Admiral owner, Bert Patrick, had a chance meeting at a cafe. There they agreed on Admiral paying Leeds £7,000 to wear a redesigned kit with the brand’s logo visible on their shirt and shorts. Patrick also secured the copyright to produce full replica kits for children, which sold for around £5.

articles.title: Xhaka promises ‘fire’ from Sunderland on long-awaited return to Europe
articles.summary: Captain looking forward to intimidating atmosphere when Wearsiders host AZ, after 53 years away. When Sunderland last played European football, club directors viewed it as a useful means of raising the cash necessary to fund floodlight upgrades at Roker Park necessitated by England’s widespread…
body: Back in the autumn of 1973 a lighting system compatible with the demands of broadcasting in black and white was proving increasingly outdated and Sunderland responded by doubling admission prices for the second leg of their opening European Cup Winners’ Cup tie against Vasas of Budapest. Coming at a moment when miners and railway workers were engaged in long-running industrial action and north-easterners’ finances were duly tight, it dictated that a disappointing crowd of under 23,000 turned out to watch Dennis Tueart’s penalty secure a 3-0 aggregate win.

Fifty-three years on, Wearside’s financial outlook is once again uncertain as the gig economy makes security a stranger for many and the cost of living spirals, but a near 49,000-capacity crowd is still expected at the Stadium of Light on Wednesday night.
Sunderland’s opening Europa League match against AZ Alkmaar will be televised across much of the world in HD but if Granit Xhaka has his way, viewers may need to adjust their brightness controls.

articles.title: Released despite seven straight wins, baffled Mokaev vows UFC return
articles.summary: Muhammad Mokaev tells BBC Sport that he is still searching for answers about why he was cut by the UFC in 2024 and dreams of returning to the organisation.
body: It has been more than two years since Muhammad Mokaev was released by the UFC - and yet he is still searching for answers.
In July 2024 the Russian-born Briton had just stretched his winning run in the promotion to seven fights with a unanimous decision victory over Manuel Kape at UFC 304.
Victory over Kape in Manchester had seemingly further cemented his place as a top contender in the flyweight division and a title shot appeared to be within his grasp.
But later that night UFC president Dana White made the shock announcement they would not be re-signing Mokaev.

articles.title: Iranian football returns in the shadow of war and with row over last league title
articles.summary: Prolonged league suspension due to war and falling behind Saudi spending power are weakening the sport in Iran. Just three months ago, Iran was one of the biggest stories in football as Team Melli arrived at the World Cup to try to play in the US, a country that had been bombing and firing missiles…
body: This week there was a return, however, to international action as Esteghlal and Tractor SC started out in the AFC Champions League Elite. It comes after the Persian Gulf League kicked off in mid-August, almost six months after it was postponed at the end of February, and subsequently abandoned as the war continued.

“The most important impact of the war on Iranian football was the prolonged suspension of competition,” the Esteghlal head coach, Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, says. “For months, we were deprived of club football, and not only were the players and teams unable to train, but the fans also had nothing to talk about, engage in banter over, and so on. It was sad that football was suspended for such a long period and it will certainly weaken the sport and its passionate supporters.”

articles.title: Sky closes in on broadcast rights for first women’s British & Irish Lions tour
articles.summary: Lions to play five fixtures in New Zealand in 2027. Sky has held live rights for men’s Lions since 1997. The inaugural women’s British & Irish Lions tour of New Zealand next year is expected to be broadcast live on Sky Sports in a significant boost for the women’s game.
body: The first women’s Lions will play three Tests against the Black Ferns and two tour matches next September, with Sky expected to broadcast all five fixtures.

Sky’s willingness to bid for the rights is a timely fillip for the sport given the disappointment expressed by Rugby Football Union officials at the BBC’s decision to limit its coverage of the Red Roses’ three home Tests this month to its red button and online channels.

The Red Roses have been regulars on BBC Two in recent years, but the main channel was showing the 1962 film Lawrence of Arabia last Saturday afternoon while the world champions were beating Australia 48-15 at Sale Sharks’ CorpAcq Stadium.
Sky’s investment in rugby union has dipped in recent years and it no longer broadcasts regular internationals or club matches, but it remains committed to its longstanding association with the Lions.

articles.title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda
articles.summary: Teenage brothers Olly and Seb Fisher are closing in on their dream of international recognition - but it won't come from their homeland of Scotland.
body: Instead, the Partick Thistle duo are in line to play for Uganda.
They believe they would become the first white players ever to represent the African nation, thanks to their mother Kate being born there.

"My gran and grandad lived out here for, I think, four or five years," Olly, 18, tells BBC Sport Scotland. "My grandfather came out here to teach in a school then my mum was born here. So, it's a bit of a strange one."
The siblings became aware of interest from Uganda about six months ago, following a chance conversation some time before between their father and a football consultant at a game in Nigeria.

articles.title: Why are Man Utd better without the ball?
articles.summary: Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball. When they have less than 50%, this number is 2.6.
body: Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average only 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball. When they have less than 50%, this number shoots up to 2.6.
And if you drop possession further, to 45% or below, United have won 10 games out of the past 10 since Carrick took the job.
It is a staggering correlation but it brings the Englishman to the same crossroads that former United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer found himself at.
How do you bridge the game from a seemingly elite counter-attacking side to one capable of beating teams that give you the ball?
points: Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball.

articles.title: Does Bellamy need to win back Wales fans?
articles.summary: After a "sleepless night", Wales boss Craig Bellamy decided to turn down the chance to manage Burnley - but has it affected what fans think of him?
body: Cristiano Ronaldo in Lisbon, Erling Haaland at home and a double-header with a Denmark side they have not beaten in 18 years as Wales return to Nations League A.
Supporters were already smarting from missing out on the World Cup. Then their mood darkened further as it emerged Bellamy had held talks over becoming boss at Burnley.

The 47-year-old admitted to a "sleepless night" when coming to a decision to either stay with Wales or succeed Scott Parker at Turf Moor, the club he had previously served as an assistant boss under Vincent Kompany.
Bellamy said he went with his gut to turn down Burnley and that he had unfinished business with his national side.

articles.title: Barcelona new arrival opens up on his instinctive style of play: ‘When I don’t think about anything…’
articles.summary: Barcelona made some very smart signings this summer, but their smartest one, considering the price, was probably Karim Adeyemi’s arrival from Borussia Dortmund. The Catalan club took advantage of the Germany star’s contractual situation and brought him in for what was a bargain price.
body: He has needed little time to show Barcelona exactly what makes him such a dangerous attacker.
The German’s game is built around explosive speed and unpredictability, but the player himself believes there is another important ingredient: instinct.
As quoted by AS, Adeyemi feels he produces his best football when he stops overthinking situations and simply reacts to what happens around him.
His performance against Levante offered a good example, including an ambitious acrobatic attempt after the ball dropped behind him.

articles.title: Stats: Aurelien Tchouameni makes instant impact in first Real Madrid start under Mourinho
articles.summary: Aurelien Tchouameni made his first start of the season for Real Madrid in Wednesday’s 3-2 win over Elche, and his return offered Jose Mourinho an early reminder of what the French midfielder can bring to the side.
body: After missing the opening part of the campaign with a pre-season injury, Tchouameni had only managed limited minutes – 11' vs Inter Milan and 21' vs Rayo Vallecano – before being trusted from the start at the Estadio Martinez Valero.

Rather than needing time to settle, the midfielder gave Real Madrid control without the ball right from the beginning, helping organise the press and closing spaces between Elche 's midfield and attack.

Tchouameni's numbers show how influential he was defensively. He finished with four recoveries, with only Trent Alexander-Arnold, Marc Cucurella and Arda Guler recording more for Real Madrid on the night.

He also made two interceptions, contributed to two blocked shots and registered six defensive actions. His two tackles showed his willingness to step into challenges, while he was not dribbled past once.

articles.title: Trio bag ultra-marathon's first women-only UK podium
articles.summary: Three women scooped the top spots in an ultra-marathon race in Derbyshire, which organisers said made it a first for the event in this country. The Rasselbock Backyard Ultra, in which competitors run a 4.16-mile course every hour, on the hour, until only one person is left standing, was held at the…
body: There were 141 competitors, and 21% of them were women and 79% men, and race organisers said this was the first occasion an all-female podium was recorded in the UK for a backyard ultra.
Matt Dillon, from Hardwick Hall, said: "Given our history and connection with Bess of Hardwick, it feels fitting that female runners made their mark on the event here."

The Hardwick Estate, now owned by the National Trust, was once home to Bess of Hardwick, who was described as a "bold businesswoman, house builder, mother and wife," and widely regarded as the second most powerful woman of the Tudor age.
Speaking about Saturday's event, Dillon added: "It promised to be an exciting event and for it to have achieved records, made it an even more memorable weekend.

articles.summary: The Listed John Musker Fillies’ Stakes takes centre stage on day two of Yarmouth’s Eastern Festival on Wednesday, all live on Sky Sports Racing.
body: The EBF Stallions John Musker Fillies' Stakes is the feature on an excellent midweek card at Yarmouth.

Simon & Ed Crisford-trained filly Fairy Glen tops the ratings with a mark of 112, and this Group Two winner could prove hard to beat in this lesser grade. She was only narrowly beaten when fifth in the Group One Prix Vicomtesse Vigier back in May and has obvious claims if fit enough on her return.
Rhapsody is a key player for William Haggas and Tom Marquand. A dual winner, she has filled the runner-up spot on her last two outings, and a similar effort would see her in the mix.

Seet is lightly-raced and should have more to offer, while Sky Safari has not been seen since finished third in the Group Three Hoppings Stakes at Newcastle and looks an each-way player on the switch to the turf.

articles.title: Inside Europe's early Ryder Cup team trip to 'immaculate' Adare Manor
articles.summary: It may still be a year to go until Team Europe's bid for a historic Ryder Cup threepeat, but Luke Donald has already had many of his prospective line-up together at Adare Manor.
body: Although not quite a full scouting mission like Donald provided ahead of previous Ryder Cup wins at Marco Simone GC and Bethpage Black, it gave many of his potential players an early experience of tackling next year's Ryder Cup venue in Ireland.

Sixteen players joined Donald and his vice-captains for the team session ahead of travelling onto the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - 10 of last year's line-up, two more with past Ryder Cup pedigree and four potential debutants.
"Any time I'm asked to go to Adare Manor, I'm going to go happily and willingly," said Jon Rahm. "It's one of the best hotel golf course experiences there is in the world.
"It was a lot of fun. It was very enjoyable. I think those days are great for all of us to see each other and just in a way remember why we do what we do.
